draft.emotion: a simple, honest expression of a personal desire, light and direct
notes: Always followed by another verb (อยาก + verb). To say you want a noun, add ได้ ('to get'): อยากได้รองเท้าคู่ใหม่ ('I want a new pair of shoes').
More casual and personal than ต้องการ, which is formal and often implies a need.

draftBefore.emotion: a simple, honest expression of a personal desire, light and direct
notes: Use 'อยาก' (yàak) to express a personal desire to do or possess something. It is a very common, everyday way to say 'I want'.
Do not confuse this with 'ต้องการ' (dtông gaan), which is more formal and often implies a need rather than a simple wish.
If you want to be more polite, you can place 'อยาก' after a polite particle like 'อยาก...ค่ะ' or 'อยาก...ครับ'.

senses.definition: To have a desire to do, perform, or experience something.

examples.text: ฉันอยากไปเที่ยวเมืองไทย
examples.translation: I want to travel to Thailand.
examples.emotion: excited, looking forward to a future plan

senses.definition: To have a desire to possess or obtain something.

examples.text: เขาอยากได้รองเท้าคู่ใหม่
examples.translation: He wants to get a new pair of shoes.
examples.emotion: determined and focused on a goal
examples.note: When followed by 'ได้' (dâai), it emphasizes the act of acquiring or getting something.

faults.quote: (possession) To have a desire to possess or obtain something.
faults.why: อยาก must be followed by a verb; 'to want a noun' requires อยากได้ (want to get).

faults.quote: you can place 'อยาก' after a polite particle like 'อยาก...ค่ะ'
faults.why: False description of word order; ค่ะ/ครับ go at the end of the sentence, after the verb phrase.
